54: /****************************************************************************
55:  * Name: bk7258_bt_bringup
56:  *
57:  * Description:
58:  *   Bluetooth transport, host registration and (optionally) the GATT
59:  *   fixture.  Deliberately NOT called from bk7258_bringup(): it only needs
60:  *   the mailbox and PWC, which bk7258_bringup() has already finished, and
61:  *   everything it does happens before the panels would otherwise light up.
62:  *   Registering the host cost the boot greeting its head start, and a radio
63:  *   that comes up a moment later is not something a user can see, whereas a
64:  *   screen that stays dark is.  Called from board_late_initialize() after
65:  *   the display instead.
66:  *
67:  *   Best-effort by the same argument: a Bluetooth failure used to abort
68:  *   bring-up and take the console, camera and panels down with it.
69:  *
70:  ****************************************************************************/
71: 
72: static void bk7258_bt_bringup(void)
73: {
74:   int ret;
75: 
76:   ret = bk7258_bt_transport_initialize();
77:   if (ret < 0)
78:     {
79:       printf("Bluetooth transport initialization failed, error=%d\n", ret);
80:       return;
81:     }
82: 
83: #  ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_BT_RAW_SELFTEST
84:   ret = bk7258_bt_raw_selftest_run();
85:   if (ret < 0)
86:     {
87:       printf("Bluetooth raw self-test failed, error=%d\n", ret);
88:     }
89: #  else
90:   ret = bk7258_bt_driver_register();
91:   if (ret < 0)
92:     {
93:       printf("Bluetooth Host registration failed, error=%d\n", ret);
94:       bk7258_bt_transport_dump_stats();
95:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
96:       return;
97:     }
98: 
99: #  ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_BT_GATT_TEST
100:   ret = bk7258_bt_gatt_test_initialize();
101:   if (ret < 0)
102:     {
103:       printf("Bluetooth GATT fixture failed, error=%d\n", ret);
104:     }
105: #  endif
106: #  endif
107: }
108: #endif
109: 
110: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDIO
111: int bk7258_mmcsd_initialize(void);
112: int bk7258_mmcsd_schedule(unsigned int delay_ms);
113: #endif
114: 
115: int bk7258_bringup(void)
116: {
117:   uint32_t button_count;
118:   int ret;
119: 
120:   button_count = board_button_initialize();
121: #ifdef CONFIG_FS_PROCFS
122:   /* Mount procfs first so that ps, free and the other informational NSH
123:    * commands work even if a later bring-up step returns early. A mount
124:    * failure is reported but never blocks bring-up: procfs is not required
125:    * by the console data path.
126:    */
127: 
128:   ret = nx_mount(NULL, "/proc", "procfs", 0, NULL);
129:   if (ret < 0)
130:     {
131:       printf("failed to mount procfs at /proc, error=%d\n", ret);
132:     }
133: #endif
134: 
135:   ret = bk7258_motor_setup();
136:   if (ret < 0)
137:     {
138:       return ret;
139:     }
140: 
141:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_link_ready(BK7258_LINK_WAIT_MS);
142:   if (ret < 0)
143:     {
144:       printf("mailbox UART0 STATE probe failed, error=%d\n", ret);
145:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
146:       bk7258_mbox_uart_dump_stats();
147:       return ret;
148:     }
149: 
150:   printf("mailbox UART0 link ready\n");
151: 
152:   ret = bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_start();
153:   if (ret < 0)
154:     {
155:       printf("HW_CTRL power-up service failed, error=%d\n", ret);
156:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
157:       return ret;
158:     }
159: 
160:   ret = bk7258_pwc_start();
161:   if (ret < 0)
162:     {
163:       return ret;
164:     }
165: 
166: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDIO
167:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_schedule(CONFIG_BK7258_SDIO_AUTOINIT_DELAY_MS);
168:   if (ret < 0)
169:     {
170:       printf("SD-NAND delayed initialization schedule failed, error=%d\n",
171:              ret);
172:     }
173: #endif
174: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI
175:   ret = bk7258_wifi_initialize();
176:   if (ret < 0)
177:     {
178:       return ret;
179:     }
180: #endif
181: 
182:   printf("button GPIOs configured, count=%lu\n",
183:          (unsigned long)button_count);
184:   printf("PWM device registered at /dev/pwm0\n");
185:   printf("mailbox transport, PWC and CPU1 ready handshake complete\n");
186:   printf("heartbeat worker started, interval=2000 ms\n");
187: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
188:   if (bk7258_psram_is_online())
189:     {
190:       printf("PSRAM online, base=0x60000000 size=0x01000000 "
191:              "RW/XN/non-cacheable\n");
192: 
193:       /* PSRAM-backed /dev/ram0: the only storage on this board big enough
194:        * to hold a captured frame as a file (tmpfs lives in the ~300KB
195:        * kernel heap, one 640x480 YUYV frame is 614400 bytes).
196:        */
197: 
198:       (void)bk7258_ramdisk_initialize();
199:       /* printf("PSRAM CP heap 0x60700000..0x6071ffff reserved\n"); */
200:       /* bk7258_psram_dump(); */
201:     }
202:   else
203:     {
204:       printf("PSRAM unavailable; media services must remain disabled\n");
205:     }
206: #endif
207: 
208: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_TRNG
209:   /* Seed the kernel entropy pool from the hardware TRNG.  Best-effort: a
210:    * probe failure leaves the pool with interrupt timing only, which is
211:    * weaker but still functional, and must not stop bring-up.  /dev/random
212:    * itself was registered earlier, by drivers_initialize().
213:    */
214: 
215:   ret = bk7258_trng_initialize();
216:   if (ret < 0)
217:     {
218:       printf("trng: initialize failed, error=%d "
219:              "(entropy pool falls back to IRQ timing)\n", ret);
220:     }
221: #endif
222: 
223:   ret = bk7258_power_key_motor_start();
224:   if (ret < 0)
225:     {
226:       return ret;
227:     }
228: 
229:   return 0;
230: }

232: /****************************************************************************
233:  * Name: bk7258_report_cache
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Reports whether this core implements instruction and data caches, and is
237:  *   left in at boot so the next person does not have to guess.
238:  *
239:  *   The AP executes in place from flash at 0x02150000.  NuttX did not enable
240:  *   the instruction cache until commit "perf(bk7258): enable the AP
241:  *   instruction cache", and every instruction fetch was a flash access: the
242:  *   expression renderer cost ~455ms per frame for work that takes 0.09ms on a
243:  *   host, a 51200-byte word-at-a-time copy ran at 0.8MB/s, and raising the
244:  *   core to 480MHz changed none of it because the core was never the limit.
245:  *   The same frame now costs 37ms.
246:  *
247:  *   Turning it on needed two independent fixes, and the first one alone looks
248:  *   like "the cache does nothing": CONFIG_ARMV8M_ICACHE depends on the hidden
249:  *   ARMV8M_HAVE_ICACHE, which this chip's Kconfig did not select, so asking
250:  *   for it in a defconfig was silently dropped; and selecting it only compiles
251:  *   up_enable_icache() in -- every other ARMv8-M chip in the tree calls that
252:  *   from its own start code, this one did not.  Both are fixed now (see the
253:  *   chip Kconfig and bk7258_start.c).
254:  *
255:  *   Only the I-Cache is on.  Instruction fetch is read-only and needs no
256:  *   maintenance against the camera, panel and mailbox DMA that shares AP RAM,
257:  *   which the MPU deliberately keeps non-cacheable.
258:  *
259:  *   CLIDR/CTR exist in ARMv8-M whether or not a cache is fitted (they read
260:  *   zero when it is not), so reading them is safe and settles the question:
261:  *   this part reports CLIDR=0x09200003, i.e. both caches are implemented.
262:  *
263:  ****************************************************************************/
264: 
265: static void bk7258_report_cache(void)
266: {
267:   uint32_t clidr = getreg32(0xe000ed78);   /* SCB->CLIDR */
268:   uint32_t ctr   = getreg32(0xe000ed7c);   /* SCB->CTR   */
269:   unsigned int l1 = clidr & 7;
270: 
271:   printf("cache: CLIDR=0x%08" PRIx32 " CTR=0x%08" PRIx32
272:          " L1=%s%s%s\n", clidr, ctr,
273:          (l1 & 1) != 0 ? "I" : "",
274:          (l1 & 2) != 0 ? "D" : "",
275:          l1 == 0 ? "none (uncached XIP from flash)" :
276:          (l1 == 3 ? " (separate I and D)" : ""));
277: }
278: 
279: void board_late_initialize(void)
280: {
281:   int ret = bk7258_bringup();
282: 
283:   bk7258_report_cache();
284: 
285:   if (ret < 0)
286:     {
287:       printf("board bring-up stopped, error=%d\n", ret);
288:       return;
289:     }
290: 
291:   printf("board bring-up initialization completed\n");
292: 
293:   /* GC9D01 QSPI panel bring-up smoke test.  board_app_finalinitialize()
294:    * (BOARDIOC_FINALINIT) is never invoked in this minimal, apps-less NSH
295:    * configuration (no CONFIG_BOARDCTL_FINALINIT, no apps/nshlib start-up
296:    * script caller), so the test entry point is invoked here instead, from
297:    * the unconditionally-called CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE hook.  See
298:    * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-gc9d01-lcd-bringup.md Task 3 Step 3.
299:    */
300: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_GC9D01_FB
301:   /* GC9D01 framebuffers, one per populated panel: fb_register() calls
302:    * up_fbinitialize(), which does the rail/reset/bus bring-up and the init
303:    * sequence and allocates a 51200-byte RGB565 framebuffer, then publishes
304:    * /dev/fb<display>.
305:    *
306:    * Both panels are registered unconditionally.  GC9D01 has no readable ID
307:    * register, so an unpopulated footprint cannot be distinguished from a
308:    * working panel -- every command still "completes".  Registering /dev/fb1
309:    * on a single-panel board therefore costs one unused 51200-byte buffer
310:    * and nothing else; refusing to register it would need board-variant
311:    * configuration that this board provides no way to detect.
312:    */
313: 
314:   {
315:     int display;
316:     int registered = 0;
317: 
318:     /* Both panels through reset and the command table in one pass, before
319:      * fb_register() asks for either of them.  The sequence is nearly all
320:      * waiting (20ms rail, 230ms reset pulse, 120ms after Sleep Out) and the
321:      * waits are the panels', not the bus's, so sharing them across the two
322:      * panels takes ~350ms off the time to the first pixel.  fb_register()
323:      * still calls up_fbinitialize() -> bk7258_gc9d01_panel_init(), which
324:      * finds its panel already up and returns.
325:      */
326: 
327:     (void)bk7258_gc9d01_panels_init((1 << GC9D01_NDISPLAYS) - 1);
328: 
329:     for (display = 0; display < GC9D01_NDISPLAYS; display++)
330:       {
331:         ret = fb_register(display, 0);
332:         if (ret < 0)
333:           {
334:             printf("fb_register(%d) failed: %d\n", display, ret);
335:             continue;
336:           }
337: 
338:         registered |= 1 << display;
339:         printf("fb: /dev/fb%d registered\n", display);
340:       }
341: 
342:     /* Boot greeting, written out rather than simply appearing.
343:      *
344:      * The panel has no readable ID register, so "the init sequence was sent"
345:      * has never been evidence that it worked; something has to be drawn at
346:      * boot or a dead panel looks exactly like a working one.
347:      *
348:      * Both panels are revealed together, one stroke segment per step, so the
349:      * word is written left to right.  The step count is the whole cost: the
350:      * panel takes no partial update, so every step pushes a full 51200-byte
351:      * frame to each panel at ~25ms, and the stroke rendering adds to that.
352:      * 20 steps measured 1677ms and was by itself most of the delay between
353:      * reset and a readable screen; 8 steps measured 408ms on the same board
354:      * and still reads as writing rather than appearing.  Keep it at 8 unless
355:      * there is a measurement to justify more.
356:      *
357:      * The pen-stroke version of this lives in the 'hello' shell command,
358:      * which has a proper stroke font.  It cannot be reused here: it is an
359:      * application, and this configuration builds neither exec_builtin() nor
360:      * posix_spawn(), so bring-up has no way to start it.
361:      */
362: 
363:     if (registered != 0)
364:       {
365:         (void)bk7258_gc9d01_fb_hello_animate(registered, 8);
366:       }
367:   }
368: #endif
369: 
370:   /* GC2145 camera: registered as a standard V4L2 /dev/video0 node here
371:    * (imgdata+imgsensor framework, see bk7258_camera_bringup.c), superseding
372:    * the older bare board_late_initialize() smoke-test call this line used
373:    * to make directly.  The old bk7258_gc2145_test() bare entry point is
374:    * kept as an independent NSH command (see bk7258_appinit.c) for
375:    * side-by-side diagnostic comparison, per design discussion in
376:    * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-gc2145-camera-bringup.md -- it is
377:    * intentionally NOT called from here anymore, so a bug in this new V4L2
378:    * driver cannot be masked by (or confused with) the old direct-call
379:    * path still running unconditionally at boot. */
380:   (void)bk7258_camera_initialize();
381: 
382: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO
383:   /* Internal-DAC audio.  This has to come after bk7258_bringup() above,
384:    * not from inside it, for the same reason the camera does: the AUD block
385:    * needs the AUDP power domain and the AUD module clock, and both are
386:    * requested from CP1 over the PWC mailbox channel that bk7258_pwc_start()
387:    * brings up.  Registering the audio devices is best-effort -- a failure
388:    * here must not take the console down with it.
389:    */
390: 
391:   (void)bk7258_audio_initialize();
392: #endif
393: 
394: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_JPEG_ENC
395:   /* After the camera: both want PSRAM, and registering the encoder second
396:    * keeps /dev/video0 belonging to capture and /dev/video1 to this codec no
397:    * matter how the framework numbers them internally.  Best-effort, like the
398:    * others -- a codec that fails to register must not take the console down.
399:    */
400: 
401:   (void)bk7258_jpeg_enc_initialize();
402: #endif
403: 
404: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_BLUETOOTH
405:   /* Last, so that nothing a user can see waits on the radio.  See
406:    * bk7258_bt_bringup() above for why this is not part of bk7258_bringup().
407:    */
408: 
409:   bk7258_bt_bringup();
410: #endif
411: }

5:  * one per QSPI controller).  Implements the three hooks fb_register() needs
6:  * -- up_fbinitialize(), up_fbgetvplane(), up_fbuninitialize() -- plus the
7:  * fb_vtable_s entries required for a panel that has no autonomous refresh:
8:  * getvideoinfo, getplaneinfo and updatearea.
9:  *
10:  * Why updatearea is mandatory here: a RAM-less RGB parallel panel is
11:  * scanned out continuously by an LCD controller, so writing the
12:  * framebuffer is enough.  GC9D01 has its own GRAM and is written over a
13:  * serial bus, so nothing reaches the glass until the driver explicitly
14:  * pushes it.  Without CONFIG_FB_UPDATE + this callback the screen would
15:  * simply never change.
16:  *
17:  * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
18:  * Multiple displays
19:  * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
20:  * fb_register(display, plane) (include/nuttx/video/fb.h) calls
21:  * up_fbinitialize(display), then up_fbgetvplane(display, plane), then
22:  * fb_register_device(), which names the node /dev/fb<display>.  So exposing
23:  * two panels is just a matter of calling fb_register() twice.
24:  *
25:  * The constraint that shapes this file: fb_vtable_s's callbacks receive
26:  * only the vtable pointer, with no display argument.  A single shared
27:  * vtable therefore cannot tell which panel it is being asked about.  Each
28:  * display consequently gets its own state structure whose *first* member is
29:  * the vtable, so a callback can recover its own state by casting the vtable
30:  * pointer back (the usual container-of trick, valid here because the vtable
31:  * sits at offset 0).
32:  *
33:  * Framebuffers come from the kernel heap: 2 x 51200 = 100KB out of roughly
34:  * 300KB, which is affordable and much faster for the CPU to write than
35:  * PSRAM (which is mapped non-cacheable).  The camera's own frame buffers do
36:  * live in PSRAM -- they are 614400 bytes each and have no alternative.
37:  *
38:  * The panels are round: the corners of the 160x160 square are not visible.
39:  * That is a composition concern for whatever draws into the framebuffer,
40:  * not something this driver compensates for.
41:  *
42:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
43:  ****************************************************************************/
44:

185: /****************************************************************************
186:  * Name: gc9d01_push
187:  *
188:  * Description:
189:  *   Re-assert the full-panel window and stream the framebuffer out.
190:  *
191:  ****************************************************************************/
192: 
193: static int gc9d01_push(FAR struct gc9d01_fb_s *priv)
194: {
195:   clock_t start = clock_systime_ticks();
196: 
197:   if (priv->fbmem == NULL || priv->bus < 0)
198:     {
199:       return -ENODEV;
200:     }
201: 
202:   if (!bk7258_gc9d01_window_full(priv->display))
203:     {
204:       return -EIO;
205:     }
206: 
207:   if (!bk7258_lcd_spi_write_frame(priv->bus, priv->fbmem, GC9D01_FBLEN))
208:     {
209:       printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: pixel burst failed\n", priv->display);
210:       return -EIO;
211:     }
212: 
213:   priv->updates++;
214: 
215:   /* First few pushes get a timing report: it is the only way to know the
216:    * real cost of a frame on this bus, which decides whether the preview
217:    * path needs DMA.  After that stay quiet -- this runs per displayed
218:    * frame.
219:    */
220: 
221:   if (priv->updates <= 3)
222:     {
223:       uint32_t ms = TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - start);
224: 
225:       printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: update %u: %d bytes in %ums "
226:              "(%u frames on bus)\n", priv->display,
227:              (unsigned int)priv->updates, GC9D01_FBLEN, (unsigned int)ms,
228:              (unsigned int)bk7258_lcd_spi_frame_count(priv->bus));
229:     }
230: 
231:   return OK;
232: }

234: #ifdef CONFIG_FB_UPDATE
235: static int gc9d01_updatearea(FAR struct fb_vtable_s *vtable,
236:                              FAR const struct fb_area_s *area)
237: {
238:   /* Partial updates would need a per-row copy out of the framebuffer,
239:    * because the panel expects a densely packed rectangle while the
240:    * framebuffer rows are GC9D01_STRIDE apart.  At 51200 bytes a full frame
241:    * is cheap enough that this always pushes everything and ignores the
242:    * requested rectangle.
243:    */
244: 
245:   UNUSED(area);
246: 
247:   if (vtable == NULL)
248:     {
249:       return -EINVAL;
250:     }
251: 
252:   return gc9d01_push(gc9d01_from_vtable(vtable));
253: }
254: #endif

260: int up_fbinitialize(int display)
261: {
262:   FAR struct gc9d01_fb_s *priv;
263:   int ret;
264: 
265:   if (display < 0 || display >= GC9D01_NDISPLAYS)
266:     {
267:       return -EINVAL;
268:     }

270:   priv = &g_gc9d01_fb[display];
271: 
272:   if (priv->fbmem == NULL)
273:     {
274:       priv->fbmem = kmm_zalloc(GC9D01_FBLEN);
275:       if (priv->fbmem == NULL)
276:         {
277:           printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: cannot allocate %d-byte framebuffer\n",
278:                  display, GC9D01_FBLEN);
279:           return -ENOMEM;
280:         }
281:     }
282: 
283:   /* Rail, panel reset, bus bring-up and the init command sequence.  Kept in
284:    * bk7258_gc9d01.c so the command table and the pin map have a single

295:     }
296: 
297:   priv->bus = bk7258_gc9d01_bus(display);

299:   printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: %dx%d RGB565, framebuffer %d bytes at %p, bus %d\n",
300:          display, GC9D01_XRES, GC9D01_YRES, GC9D01_FBLEN, priv->fbmem,

322:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_fb_fill
323:  *
324:  * Description:
325:  *   Bring-up helper: fills one display's framebuffer with a solid RGB565
326:  *   colour and pushes it.  This is the first thing that can prove the whole
327:  *   chain (bus framing, init sequence, CASET/RASET, pixel burst) actually
328:  *   reaches the glass -- the panel has no readable ID register, so until
329:  *   something is visible there is no evidence the init sequence worked.
330:  *
331:  ****************************************************************************/

333: int bk7258_gc9d01_fb_fill(int display, uint16_t rgb565)
334: {
335:   FAR struct gc9d01_fb_s *priv;
336:   FAR uint16_t *px;
337:   int i;
338: 
339:   if (display < 0 || display >= GC9D01_NDISPLAYS)
340:     {
341:       return -EINVAL;
342:     }
343: 
344:   priv = &g_gc9d01_fb[display];
345:   px = (FAR uint16_t *)priv->fbmem;
346: 
347:   if (px == NULL)
348:     {

362: /****************************************************************************
363:  * Name: greeting_style
364:  *
365:  * Description:
366:  *   The pen and layout the boot greeting is drawn with.  These are the same
367:  *   numbers as 'hello em=52 thick=4', so the boot animation and the shell
368:  *   command produce the same strokes -- they now share one renderer
369:  *   (hello_paint.c) and one stroke font (hello_font.c) instead of the panel
370:  *   driver carrying its own 5x7 bitmap copy of the word.
371:  *
372:  ****************************************************************************/
373: 
374: #define GC9D01_GREETING_TEXT   "hello vela"
375: #define GC9D01_GREETING_EM     52
376: #define GC9D01_GREETING_THICK  4
377: #define GC9D01_GREETING_STEPS  20
378: 
379: static int32_t greeting_style(FAR struct hs_style_s *st)
380: {
381:   int32_t budget = (GC9D01_XRES * 16 * 85) / 100;
382:   int32_t width = 0;
383:   int32_t total;
384: 
385:   memset(st, 0, sizeof(*st));
386:   st->fg      = 0xffff;
387:   st->bg      = 0x0000;
388:   st->em16    = GC9D01_GREETING_EM * 16;
389:   st->thick16 = GC9D01_GREETING_THICK * 16;
390: 
391:   /* Baseline is nudged below the centre by the same fraction the command
392:    * uses, so the word sits optically centred rather than mathematically.
393:    */
394: 
395:   st->baseline16 = (GC9D01_YRES * 16) / 2 + (st->em16 * 10) / 64;
396:   total = hs_measure(GC9D01_GREETING_TEXT, st, &width);
397: 
398:   /* Auto-fit, same 85% chord budget as the shell command.  The glass is
399:    * round, so the usable width is a chord rather than the full 160 pixels,
400:    * and GC9D01_GREETING_EM is the requested size rather than a promise: at
401:    * em 52 "hello vela" is about 180 pixels wide and would lose its first
402:    * letter off the left edge, which looks like a font bug rather than an
403:    * overflow.
404:    */
405: 
406:   if (width > budget && width > 0)
407:     {
408:       st->em16 = (st->em16 * budget) / width;
409:       st->thick16 = (st->thick16 * budget) / width;
410: 
411:       if (st->thick16 < 2 * 16)
412:         {
413:           st->thick16 = 2 * 16;
414:         }
415: 
416:       st->baseline16 = (GC9D01_YRES * 16) / 2 + (st->em16 * 10) / 64;
417:       total = hs_measure(GC9D01_GREETING_TEXT, st, &width);
418:     }
419: 
420:   st->cx16 = (GC9D01_XRES * 16 - width) / 2;
421:   return total;
422: }

619:     }
620: 
621:   memset(&fmt, 0, sizeof(fmt));
622:   fmt.type                = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
623:   fmt.fmt.pix.width       = CAM_WIDTH;
624:   fmt.fmt.pix.height      = CAM_HEIGHT;

627:   /* The real memory layout is V Y1 U Y0 (see preview_convert()), which no

629:    * pair, and the imgsensor/imgdata layers this driver sits on define only
630:    * UYVY and YUYV anyway.  UYVY is therefore what both sides agree to call
631:    * it -- a label for "packed 4:2:2, chroma first", with the exact order
632:    * documented in the driver and decoded by preview_convert().  Agreeing
633:    * with the driver is necessary (VIDIOC_S_FMT fails otherwise) but not
634:    * sufficient: both sides can be wrong in the same direction without any

655:     }

657:   p->nbuffers = req.count < NBUFFERS ? req.count : NBUFFERS;

661:       memset(&buf, 0, sizeof(buf));

694: ## 8. 线程、优先级与内存路线
695: 
696: 首版建议 6 个执行上下文，具体优先级按最终系统负载实测调整：
697: 
698: | 上下文 | 职责 | 规则 |
699: | --- | --- | --- |
700: | App 主线程 | 状态机和事件消费 | 不做阻塞网络、文件大读写或整帧转换 |
701: | Input worker | 10 ms 按键扫描 | 小栈、固定周期，不打印高频日志 |
702: | Media worker | Camera/Audio 采集和排队 | 音频路径优先，图片队列满时丢最旧帧 |
703: | Voice worker | VAD、ASR/Agent 请求和流式 TTS 编排 | 与社交模式互斥；每个阻塞步骤都检查取消 generation |
704: | Cloud worker | TLS、上传、接收和 finalize 轮询 | 所有请求有超时和取消令牌 |
705: | Display worker | 生成两块帧缓冲并提交 | 事件驱动；同屏短时间多次更新合并为一次 |
706: 
707: Storage 可先由 Cloud worker 在 finalizing 阶段串行执行，只有实测写入阻塞影响音频或 UI
708: 时才拆出第七个 worker。闲时语音助手和社交辅助模式互斥占用 Camera、ADC、DAC 与云请求
709: 上下文；切换前必须先停止并释放上一模式的全部媒体资源。
710: 
711: 内存原则：
712: 
713: - 两块显示前台 framebuffer 已由驱动持有；App 最多再持有一块 51200 B 绘制缓冲并串行
714:   更新两屏，优先于额外保留两块后台缓冲。
715: - JPEG 和 PCM 使用 PSRAM 有界池，不用无上限 `malloc` 链表。
716: - 语音问答优先使用流式 ASR；若首版云接口只能整包上传，则 PCM 使用 PSRAM 有界 ring，
717:   达到上限自动截断，绝不扩容越界。
718: - ADC 录音与 DAC/TTS 默认不并发。开始播报前关闭录音；取消播报调用
719:   `audio_playback_stop()` 并关闭仍在下载的响应。
720: - JSON 使用流式或有上限解析；最终记录允许落临时文件，不要求整包永久驻留 SRAM。
721: - UI 快照使用定长短文本，不引用网络接收缓冲生命周期之外的指针。
722: - Camera、Audio、网络和显示关闭流程必须可重复调用，以便错误回滚。

**Repository Findings**

The relevant participant project is:

[contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing)

It contains:

- A working dual-panel framebuffer board implementation.
- A working `camera_preview` application.
- A working `social_cue` application.
- An implemented but currently empty `app/velasight` skeleton.
- A boot-time hello animation implemented in board code.
- No completed registration or autostart path for `velasight`.

The repository was inspected read-only. No files were changed.

## 1. Existing Applications

### `camera_preview`

Source:

- [app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c)

- [app/camera_preview/preview_jpeg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/preview_jpeg.h)

The materialized package is currently visible at:

#### Application registration



The current `LVX_USE_DEMO_*` naming is a local naming convention. It does not imply that the application uses LVGL.

#### Framebuffer APIs used by `camera_preview`

Panel discovery and mapping are implemented in [camera_preview_main.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:520):

```c
open("/dev/fb0", O_RDWR);
open("/dev/fb1", O_RDWR);

ioctl(fd, FBIOGET_VIDEOINFO, (uintptr_t)&p->vinfo);
ioctl(fd, FBIOGET_PLANEINFO, (uintptr_t)&p->pinfo);

mmap(NULL,
     p->pinfo.fblen,
     PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
     MAP_SHARED | MAP_FILE,
     fd,
     0);
```

Important properties:

- It probes both `/dev/fb0` and `/dev/fb1`.
- Missing panels are tolerated when both-panel mode is requested.
- It validates `FB_FMT_RGB16_565`.
- It uses `pinfo.stride` and `pinfo.fblen`.
- The framebuffer is directly writable from user space.
- The application keeps one mapped framebuffer per display.

Updates are committed using:

```c
struct fb_area_s area;

area.x = 0;
area.y = 0;
area.w = p->vinfo.xres;
area.h = p->vinfo.yres;

ioctl(fd, FBIO_UPDATE, (uintptr_t)&area);
```

The helper is at [camera_preview_main.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:1605).

Although the API accepts an area, the board driver currently pushes a full frame for every update. Partial updates are deliberately ignored by the driver.

#### Camera APIs used

The camera path opens:

```c
open("/dev/video0", O_RDWR);
```

It configures V4L2:

```c
VIDIOC_S_FMT
VIDIOC_REQBUFS
VIDIOC_QUERYBUF
VIDIOC_QBUF
VIDIOC_STREAMON
VIDIOC_DQBUF
VIDIOC_STREAMOFF
```

The implementation uses:

```c
V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE
V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP
V4L2_PIX_FMT_UYVY
```

The relevant setup begins at [camera_preview_main.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:607).

It requests 640x480 packed 4:2:2 capture, maps the V4L2 buffers, converts into RGB565, and writes directly to the mapped framebuffer.

Supported modes include:

- `camera_preview fill f800`
- `camera_preview bars`
- `camera_preview grid`
- `camera_preview pattern`
- `camera_preview face`
- `camera_preview live+face`
- `camera_preview live+face 40`
- `camera_preview live+face 120 src=/mnt/expr.txt`
- `camera_preview jpeg`
- `camera_preview jpegb64`
- `camera_preview fb=0`
- `camera_preview fb=1`
- `camera_preview fb=both`

Argument parsing is at [camera_preview_main.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:1857).

The `live+face` implementation intentionally assigns different work to the two panels:

- One panel receives the live camera preview every frame.
- The other panel receives a rendered expression only when the expression changes.

## 2. Dual `/dev/fb0` and `/dev/fb1` Implementation

Board framebuffer headers:

- [bk7258_gc9d01_fb.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.h)
- [bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c)
- [bk7258_gc9d01.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01.c)

The board constants are:

[gc9d01_fb.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.h:20):

```c
#define GC9D01_NDISPLAYS 2
#define GC9D01_XRES      160
#define GC9D01_YRES      160
#define GC9D01_BPP       16
#define GC9D01_STRIDE    (GC9D01_XRES * 2)
#define GC9D01_FBLEN     (GC9D01_STRIDE * GC9D01_YRES)
```

Thus each framebuffer is:

```text
160 x 160
RGB565
2 bytes per pixel
stride = 320 bytes
fblen = 51,200 bytes
```

The board allocates two kernel-heap framebuffers, approximately 100 KiB total.

The driver implements:

```c
up_fbinitialize(int display)
up_fbgetvplane(int display, int vplane)
up_fbuninitialize(int display)
```

The framebuffer vtable contains:

```c
getvideoinfo
getplaneinfo
updatearea
```

The relevant definitions are in [bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c:86).

Each display has an independent vtable/state object because `fb_vtable_s` callbacks do not receive a display index. The driver uses the vtable’s position as the first member of `struct gc9d01_fb_s` to recover the per-display state.

The framebuffer nodes are registered in [bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:314):

```c
bk7258_gc9d01_panels_init((1 << GC9D01_NDISPLAYS) - 1);

for (display = 0; display < GC9D01_NDISPLAYS; display++)
  {
    ret = fb_register(display, 0);
  }
```

`fb_register(0, 0)` publishes `/dev/fb0`; `fb_register(1, 0)` publishes `/dev/fb1`.

The board Kconfig option is:

[bk7258-ap/Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:18):

```kconfig
config BK7258_GC9D01_FB
    bool "GC9D01 panel framebuffer (/dev/fb0)"
    default n
    depends on VIDEO_FB
    select FB_UPDATE
```

The comment says `/dev/fb0`, but the implementation registers both `/dev/fb0` and `/dev/fb1`.

The board source registration is:

[board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/CMakeLists.txt](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/CMakeLists.txt:21):

```cmake

  list(APPEND SRCS bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c
    hello_paint.c
    hello_font.c)
endif()
```

The legacy Make equivalent is:

[board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/Makefile](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/Makefile:16):

```make
CSRCS += bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c hello_paint.c hello_font.c
endif
```

### Important update behavior

`gc9d01_updatearea()` ignores the requested rectangle:

[bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c:234)

```c
return gc9d01_push(gc9d01_from_vtable(vtable));
```

`gc9d01_push()`:

1. Reasserts the full CASET/RASET panel window.
2. Sends all 51,200 bytes over the LCD bus.
3. Does not perform partial row extraction.

Therefore the first-stage UI should:

- Render into the mapped framebuffer.
- Coalesce related state changes.
- Issue one `FBIO_UPDATE` per changed display.
- Avoid per-widget or per-pixel updates.
- Avoid continuous animation unless measured and explicitly needed.

The project’s own design plan states the same constraint:

[VELASIGHT_MCU_APP_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/VELASIGHT_MCU_APP_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:50):

> `/dev/fb0`、`/dev/fb1`，160x160，RGB565，各 51200 B；无局部刷新，状态变化后整帧提交；避免持续动画

### Recommendation on LVGL

For a first-stage VelaSight UI, do not introduce LVGL yet.

Reasons:

1. The board framebuffer is already functional.
2. The panel is only 160x160 RGB565.
3. There is no partial refresh.
4. Existing working applications already render directly into the framebuffer.
5. LVGL is disabled in the relevant generated configuration.
6. Introducing LVGL requires deciding how its display driver maps to two independent framebuffer devices and how its flush callback handles the full-frame `FBIO_UPDATE` cost.
7. The existing product plan already calls for a small direct RGB565 renderer.

LVGL can be reconsidered later if the UI grows to require:

- Complex focus navigation.
- Large widget inventories.
- Text layout and font management.
- Animation scheduling.
- Input device integration.
- Reusable theme/layout support.

For stage one, a small `vs_display.c` renderer with fixed-size text, icons, status bars, progress arcs, and explicit frame commits is the lower-risk path.

## 5. Hello Animation and Boot Ordering

The actual boot greeting is not started by the `hello_screen` application.

The boot animation is implemented directly in board code:

[board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:279)

```c
void board_late_initialize(void)
```

The ordering is:

```text
board_late_initialize()
  -> bk7258_bringup()
  -> panel initialization
  -> fb_register(0, 0)       publishes /dev/fb0
  -> fb_register(1, 0)       publishes /dev/fb1
  -> bk7258_gc9d01_fb_hello_animate(registered, 8)
  -> bk7258_camera_initialize()
  -> optional audio initialization
  -> optional JPEG encoder initialization
  -> optional Bluetooth initialization
  -> return
  -> NSH startup / init scripts
```

The critical sequence is at [bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:300):

```c
bk7258_gc9d01_panels_init(...);

for (display = 0; display < GC9D01_NDISPLAYS; display++)
  {
    ret = fb_register(display, 0);
  }

if (registered != 0)
  {
    (void)bk7258_gc9d01_fb_hello_animate(registered, 8);
}
```

The camera is initialized only after the animation:

[bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:370)


This means `/dev/fb0` and `/dev/fb1` are available before the animation begins, and they remain available after `board_late_initialize()` returns.

The animation function is:

Declared in:

[bk7258_gc9d01_fb.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.h:106)

The current generated NSH configuration shows:

[out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:1991)


It also shows:

And:

[out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:2154)


The important distinction is:

- `CONFIG_NSH_INITSCRIPT` points NSH at an `rcS` script.
- `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_APPS` controls whether application commands are available to NSH.
- The generated `nsh` configuration currently does not include builtin apps.
- Therefore a normal `rcS` command such as `velasight &` cannot work until the builtin application path is enabled and the application is registered.

The participant source does not contain a visible `rcS` implementation or a `velasight` autostart command. The current board code only starts the hello animation and board drivers.

The project’s general boot documentation describes the expected order:

[docs/en/device_dev_guide/kernel/boot_process.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/docs/en/device_dev_guide/kernel/boot_process.md:21):

```text
board_late_initialize()
  -> rc.sysinit
  -> board_app_finalinitialize()
  -> rcS
```

For this board’s current configuration, the practical ordering is:

```text
board_late_initialize()
  -> register framebuffers
  -> run hello animation synchronously
  -> initialize camera
  -> return
  -> NSH starts
  -> rcS can start user applications
```

That makes `rcS` the cleanest application-level point for starting VelaSight after the greeting.

## 7. Recommended Minimal First-Stage Approach

### Recommendation

Implement VelaSight as a normal builtin NuttX application using direct framebuffer rendering, then launch it from `rcS` after `board_late_initialize()` has completed.

The minimal architecture should be:

```text
board_late_initialize()
  -> register fb0/fb1
  -> run hello animation
  -> initialize camera
  -> return

NSH startup
  -> rcS
  -> start velasight
       -> open fb0/fb1
       -> mmap both framebuffer buffers
       -> render initial UI
       -> FBIO_UPDATE each changed screen
       -> run event/state loop
```

This provides the desired ordering without making board code depend directly on an application entry point.

### Why this is preferable

- The hello animation remains board-owned and synchronous.
- VelaSight starts only after the animation returns.
- The application does not need to duplicate panel initialization.
- The application uses the public framebuffer device API.
- The board layer does not need to call `task_create()` on an application-specific function.
- NSH/`rcS` naturally handles application startup.
- The application can be independently launched from the console for testing.
- The application can be stopped and restarted without rebooting the board.

### Minimal display implementation

`vs_display.c` should initially do only the following:

1. Open `/dev/fb0`.
2. Open `/dev/fb1`.
3. Query each with:
   - `FBIOGET_VIDEOINFO`
   - `FBIOGET_PLANEINFO`
4. Check:
   - `FB_FMT_RGB16_565`
   - `xres == 160`
   - `yres == 160`
   - expected stride/fblen
5. Map each framebuffer with `mmap()`.
6. Clear and draw each screen in CPU memory.
7. Submit each changed display with:
   - `FBIO_UPDATE`
8. Close/unmap cleanly on shutdown or error.

Suggested internal representation:

```c
struct vs_panel_s
{
    int fd;
    int index;
    struct fb_videoinfo_s vinfo;
    struct fb_planeinfo_s pinfo;
    FAR uint16_t *pixels;
    bool dirty;
};
```

The app can use the framebuffer-owned memory directly. The plan’s suggestion of an additional single drawing buffer is optional for the first stage. Avoid allocating two extra 51,200-byte buffers unless there is a measured need.

### Minimal first-stage screens

Use fixed-size, direct RGB565 drawing:

- `fb0`: primary state/index screen.
- `fb1`: secondary summary/status screen.

A minimal initial state set could be:

```text
HOME
LIST
DETAIL
PAUSED
ERROR
```

Initially implement:

- Solid background.
- Fixed bitmap or stroke-font text.
- A few simple icons.
- A status color band.
- A progress ring or bar.
- One or two lines of bounded text.
- Full-frame update only after a complete screen composition.

Do not begin with camera streaming inside VelaSight. First prove:

```text
velasight starts after hello
fb0 renders
fb1 renders
button/event loop works
state transitions work
```

Then add camera/media integration.

### Event and rendering loop

The first-stage loop should be event-driven:

```text
input/event arrives
  -> update state
  -> generate framebuffer contents
  -> mark changed panel(s)
  -> submit only changed panel(s)
  -> wait for next event
```

Do not refresh at a fixed high rate. Every display update transmits a complete frame over the serial panel bus.

The product plan already recommends a display worker that coalesces updates:

[VELASIGHT_MCU_APP_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/VELASIGHT_MCU_APP_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:705):

> Display worker: 生成两块帧缓冲并提交；事件驱动；同屏短时间多次更新合并为一次

For a minimal implementation, this can initially be the main application thread rather than a separate display worker.

## 8. Autostart Recommendation

### Preferred application-level path

Enable the VelaSight builtin application and launch it from the board’s `rcS` startup script:

```text
velasight &
```

The exact script source needs to be identified or added in the board configuration that produces:

```text
CONFIG_NSH_INITSCRIPT="init.d/rcS"
```

The required configuration direction is:

```text
CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_APPS=y
CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_VELASIGHT=y
CONFIG_BK7258_GC9D01_FB=y
CONFIG_VIDEO_FB=y
CONFIG_FB_UPDATE=y
```

The last two framebuffer symbols are already conceptually connected through the board Kconfig:

```kconfig
config BK7258_GC9D01_FB
    depends on VIDEO_FB
    select FB_UPDATE
```

`velasight` should open the devices only after it starts. It should not call `fb_register()` itself.

### What should not be done for stage one

Avoid directly calling `velasight_main()` from:

```text
board_late_initialize()
```

Reasons:

- It couples board code to application code.
- It risks running application logic in the board bring-up task.
- It complicates startup failure handling.
- It makes the app harder to run manually.
- It is contrary to the existing comment in `bk7258_bringup.c`, which explicitly notes that applications cannot be started there in the minimal configuration because the builtin/spawn paths are disabled.

Avoid starting a long-running UI loop synchronously in `board_late_initialize()`. The board hook should finish after hardware registration, hello animation, and driver initialization.

### Alternative if `rcS` cannot be enabled

If the target image intentionally remains a minimal no-builtin NSH configuration, the fallback is a board-owned launcher task created after:

```c
bk7258_gc9d01_fb_hello_animate(registered, 8);
```

However, this should be treated as a second choice. It would require:

- A board-visible launcher function.
- A task entry point.
- Cross-layer linkage between board code and application code.
- A decision about whether the task executes the app’s real `main()` or a separate app-start wrapper.
- Careful handling of the board task’s stack and lifetime.

The cleaner first-stage path remains:

```text
board_late_initialize() completes
rcS starts velasight
```

## 9. Concrete Minimal Scope

The smallest useful first-stage implementation should consist of:

1. Register `app/velasight` using the existing four-file application pattern.
2. Add the manifest link into `packages/demos`.
3. Implement `velasight_main.c` as a builtin entry point.
4. Implement `vs_display.c` using the proven `camera_preview` framebuffer APIs.
5. Open and map both `/dev/fb0` and `/dev/fb1`.
6. Render one static initial screen on each display.
7. Submit each with full-screen `FBIO_UPDATE`.
8. Add a small event/state loop.
9. Enable `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_APPS`.
10. Start `velasight &` from `rcS`.
11. Verify boot ordering:
    - hello animation completes,
    - `board_late_initialize()` continues,
    - NSH starts,
    - `velasight` starts,
    - VelaSight overwrites the hello frame on both panels.
